sources.decisions.benefit_decision.pension: Review: an authorised review officer of Services Australia reviews the decision on request, within 13 weeks (91 days) of it (Social Security (Administration) Act 1999, ss 111 and 129: recalled, to confirm); appeal to the Administrative Review Tribunal within 13 weeks of the review decision, no fee for a social security matter (the same Act, s 142, and the Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024: recalled, to confirm); an appeal lies only after the review. The 14 days to send the documents a claim needs: recalled from Services Australia's guidance to claimants (to confirm).
sources.decisions.benefit_decision.unemployment: As the Age Pension (review and appeal: recalled, to confirm). The employer's confirmation that the job has ended is the employment separation certificate Services Australia asks a JobSeeker claimant to have their employer complete (recalled, to confirm); its 14 days is a PLACEHOLDER, and the claim is decided without it if it does not come.
sources.culture.conducts: What people start out holding right, for the four conducts where a figure in this profile's own outlook speaks to it (the rest start from values alone: no figure was opened). approves_bps is the national share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence, as `outlook.trust` has it (World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7, as Our World in Data publishes it; opened 2026-10-11, to confirm against the survey's tables; see sources.outlook for the country and the items). Mapping, ours: answer_tribunal and take_to_tribunal <- confidence in the courts (a person who trusts the courts approves of answering a case there and of taking a wrong to it); complain <- confidence in the civil service (writing to the town is approved where the town's officers are trusted to answer); join_union <- confidence in labour unions. Weak: confidence in an institution is not approval of an act toward it, and the share above a threshold is read as a mean, as outlook does; the figure sets where people start (their own lean and their picture of what others approve), nothing else, and the lean is measured from it, so the rates stay the calibrated ones. No figure for strike, take_in, stay_past_notice, take_from_employer or an organisation's conduct (the survey's items on joining strikes and on the justifiability of stealing property were not opened); no figure by origin group (no source found that gives one). National, not the place's. does_bps is never given: a conduct's own rate in the profile.
sources.culture.origin: PLACE: Victoria (the state), 2021. groups: ABS Census 2021 QuickStats, Victoria, country of birth (ABS, 2021), https://www.abs.gov.au/census/find-census-data/quickstats/2021/2 , OPENED 2026-10-13: born in Australia 65.0% (4,228,667), India 4.0%, England 2.7%, China 2.6%, New Zealand 1.5%, Vietnam 1.4%; 'all other' is the remainder (22.8%), including not stated; shares rounded to basis points. same_household_bps: 7500 = the share of couples with both partners born in the same country, 75% in 2017, from the HILDA Survey (Melbourne Institute, released 2019) as reported in The Conversation, 'Language of love: a quarter of Australians are in inter-ethnic relationships', https://theconversation.com/language-of-love-a-quarter-of-australians-are-in-inter-ethnic-relationships-120416 , OPENED 2026-10-13 (the article, not the HILDA tables; 56% of couples had both partners born in Australia). National, not Victoria; Victoria has fewer Australian-born (65.0% against 66.9%), so the share here is probably a little lower (to confirm). homophily_bps: PLACEHOLDER 5000 (a close tie is half again as likely within a group as by chance). No survey of close ties or friendship by group for this place was found and opened; McPherson, Smith-Lovin and Cook 2001 ('Birds of a feather', Annual Review of Sociology 27) gives the general fact, not this place's figure. CHILDREN: the census counts each person by their own country of birth (and has separate questions on parents' birthplaces), so a child born in Australia to a mixed couple is counted Australian-born whatever the parents' countries: the generator's rule (either parent's group, equal chance) does not match this source for the birth-country classes. To confirm against ABS 'Country of birth of parents'.
sources.tenancy.rent_share_of_income: PLACEHOLDER bands around one opened mean: private renters' housing costs averaged 20.2% of gross household income in 2019-20; lower-income private renters averaged 32%, and 58% of them paid over 30% (ABS, Housing Occupancy and Costs, 2019-20, https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/housing/housing-occupancy-and-costs/latest-release, release page opened 2026-10-12; national). The bands themselves (56% under a fifth, 23% a fifth to three tenths, 15% three tenths to a half, 6% over a half) were NOT read: they are in the release's data cubes 4, 8 and 13, which were not opened. To replace from cube 4. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): each renting household of a new town draws its share from these bands (evenly within a band; the open band from its lower bound to twice it, at most everything), which gives the rent it carries; households and let homes are matched by it. A target as well: the town's own distribution at the start is reported beside it and is not fitted to it.
sources.support.take_up_bps: pension 64%: DERIVED from an opened page: on 28 March 2025, 62% of people aged 65 and over received income support and 91% of those the Age Pension, so about 56% of those 65 and over (26% at 65-69, 59% at 70-79, 80% at 85 and over; AIHW, Australia's welfare, Income support for older Australians, https://www.aihw.gov.au/reports/australias-welfare/income-support-older-australians, opened 2026-10-12); the pension starts at 67, so the two years before it are taken out of the denominator by a rough twelfth (to confirm against DSS payment demographics by single age). The real pension is means-tested and the profile's is not: those not drawing it here claim it on the first day and are granted. unemployment 50%: PLACEHOLDER: no ratio of JobSeeker recipients to the unemployed was found. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Payments in force"): of those the payment's rule already entitles as the year begins, this share open with it in payment; the rest claim it when they first look, as before.
sources.ownership.owner_bps_by_age: Home ownership by age of the household reference person, Census 2021, national: 36% at 25-29, 50% at 30-34, 72% at 50-54 (AIHW, Australia's welfare, Home ownership and housing tenure, https://www.aihw.gov.au/reports/australias-welfare/home-ownership-and-housing-tenure, opened 2026-10-12); 79.4% at 65 and over (a search summary of ABS Census 2021 reporting: to confirm). The bands between are not filled: 35 to 49 is read at the 30-34 figure and under 30 at the 25-29 figure, which understates both. To replace from the Census table by ten-year bands. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): only as how much likelier a household of one age is than another to be among the town's owners; their number is the houses the profile's house_owner_bps makes owner-occupied.
sources.households.kin_households_most_bps: PLACEHOLDER 3%: the census category (multiple-family households) is published only in tables that could not be read; what was opened is 'other family' households, 0.94% in the rest of Victoria, a different category (ABS, Census 2021, G42 through the ABS Data API, opened 2026-10-12). To source: ABS Census 2021, household composition, multiple-family households. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/households.md, "Taken in"): a ceiling and nothing else: no more households than this hold kin when people with nothing coming in are placed with a household that can carry them.
sources.tenancy.possession: Residential Tenancies Act 1997 (Vic): a notice to vacate may be given once rent is 14 days or more in arrears, of 14 days (Consumer Affairs Victoria, Late or unpaid rent: opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11, for the 14 days' arrears, that paying by the date ends the notice, that the rental provider must then apply to VCAT, that payment plans can be ordered, and that only the police carry out an order; the 14-day notice period, s 91ZM and ss 330 to 331 to confirm). possession_days 14, plan_months 6 and warrant_days 14 (a warrant of possession is to be executed within 14 days of issue: to confirm) are PLACEHOLDERS for VCAT's practice. The two shares of how tenants answer are the same in every profile: stay_past_notice_bps 5000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for the share of tenants who stay past a notice for arrears); leave_on_order_bps 5900 is England's, used everywhere: of 16,848 landlord possession orders in January to March 2026, 6,888 repossessions were by county court bailiffs, 41%, so about 59% of those ordered out were gone without one (Ministry of Justice, Mortgage and Landlord Possession Statistics, January to March 2026: opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11; a ratio of one quarter's flows, not of one cohort). eviction_notice_days: the notice of the day that whoever carries out a warrant gives the tenant; England's county court bailiffs give 14 days' notice of an eviction (Civil Procedure Rules 83.8A: to confirm, recalled), Germany's Gerichtsvollzieher about three weeks (to confirm); every other place's figure is a PLACEHOLDER (7 days; Ohio 3, within its ten). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/justice.md, "Possession"): published in the town as a law; a landlord gives a notice to vacate under it, applies to the tribunal if the tenant stays, and asks for a warrant if they stay past its order; the tribunal sets a plan or a date by it; the police carry the warrant out. Tenants who answer, and plans (2026-10-12): answer_bps 4300: the renter attended, or someone attended for them, at 43% of 822 hearings observed in 2023 ('Key Findings: VCAT hearing observations dataset', opened by a research agent 2026-10-12; applicants were the housing authority and community housing providers, so social and not private landlords; its publisher was not found: to confirm; older Victorian figures it cites run from 20% to 28% for private renters, secondary). plan_consider 'must': the tribunal must be satisfied that possession is reasonable and proportionate, and may adjourn or dismiss an application for arrears where other arrangements can be made (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 'Evictions and possession orders', opened 2026-10-12; the sections, Residential Tenancies Act 1997 ss 330A and 331, recalled, to confirm).
sources.business.entry_bps_per_year: ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, including Entries and Exits, 2024-25: 437,150 entries on about 2.66 million businesses at the start, 16.4% (the profile's target of the same name); 2025-26: 16.9% entries, 13.8% exits, and 64.6% of businesses have no employees (opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11). National; Victoria's own rate not retrieved. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/entry.md, "Starting a business of one"): the generator turns it into a monthly chance for those who could start a business of one (in the labour force, of working age, with the savings for its stock), from the businesses the town has: births a year at this rate, over those people. Most real births are businesses with no employees, which is the only kind that can be started here without premises.
sources.business.trade_credit_days: PLACEHOLDER 30 days, to confirm: the ordinary terms on which a supplier gives a business time to pay for goods delivered (an invoice due in 30 days is the common term in Australian business-to-business trade; the Payment Times Reporting Scheme (Payment Times Reporting Act 2020 (Cth)) has large businesses report the days they take to pay small ones, and the Commonwealth's own policy is payment of small business invoices within 20 days; recalled, not opened, for this work). Used for factories selling to shops and the outside world selling inputs to factories (docs/behaviour/trade.md, "Trade credit").
sources.employment.hours: Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth): ordinary hours are a maximum of 38 a week (s 62), and a change to an employee's hours needs the employee's agreement or an award, enterprise agreement or contract term that allows it; s 524 lets an employer stand an employee down without pay only for industrial action, equipment breakdown or a stoppage the employer cannot reasonably be held responsible for, and a want of ordinary trade is not clearly one (to confirm: legislation.gov.au would not open; read from search results 2026-10-13). So here: only with the employee's agreement, any hours, no spell limit, pay for the hours worked only. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Hours before heads"): published in the town as a law (law-cutting-hours); a shop or factory over its need cuts everyone's hours to what its trade needs before it lets anyone go, where this says it may, and pays what it owes for the hours cut; a worker reads the employer's paper as the pay agreed. consent_bps 9000 is a PLACEHOLDER (of workers asked to agree to a cut as the alternative to someone being let go, the share who do; no figure found). The employer's own notice of 3 days is ours, so that the paper reaches the worker first.
sources.employment.adjustment: PLACEHOLDERS, the same in every profile, with a sourced shape (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"; docs/research/references.md). smooth_months 3: firms plan production and workforce on smoothed, forecast trade and not on the last period's (Holt, Modigliani, Muth and Simon 1960); no figure for the horizon of a small employer here was found. hiring_cost_weeks 8: what recruiting and training a new worker costs, in weeks of their pay; estimates run from under two weeks to over sixteen (Silva and Toledo 2009; Manning 2011; Blatter, Muehlemann and Schenker 2012; Muehlemann and Leiser 2018: all to confirm, none opened), and none is for this place.
sources.employment.termination: Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth) s 117 (notice: 1 week under a year's service, 2 from one year, 3 from three, 4 from five; a further week for those over 45 with two years is left out), s 119 (redundancy pay: 4 weeks from one year, rising to 16 at nine years and 12 from ten), s 121 (none owed by an employer of fewer than 15) (to confirm: recalled by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11, the statute not opened). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"): published in the town as a law; an employer reads it before letting someone go for redundancy (what it would owe is part of what the job costs to end) and pays what it says when the job ends. Service is counted from the start of a run: nobody's earlier years with an employer are known to it.
sources.frictions: Everyday frictions (docs/behaviour/frictions.md): what goes wrong, how often, and how the bodies that hear it work. Read by the generator only for a town whose spec has `living`.
sources.frictions.per_adult_bps_per_year: Of adults, the share who had each kind of problem, a year: half the share who had it in the last two years in World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only). landlord: a problem with a landlord over agreements, payments, repairs, deposits or eviction (12.8% in two years; all of it is given to disrepair here, which overstates repairs: the town has no other landlord problem of the kind yet). wages: difficulty obtaining wages or employment benefits agreed in advance (8.4%). bill: major disruption of a utility's supply or incorrect billing (21.6%; all of it is given to wrong bills). benefits: difficulty obtaining public benefits or government assistance (12.0%). goods: a consumer problem (38.1%) less the utility share, since the survey's consumer problems include it (derived; poor professional services are in it too). The generator turns each into a rate for those exposed (a let dwelling, a job, a customer, a claim) with the town's own counts. Halving a two-year share understates a yearly one where people have a problem in both years (to confirm against a yearly survey). Cross-checks for Victoria (docs/research/references.md): 28% of renters reported an issue with their rental provider in a year and 13% had it unresolved (Consumer Policy Research Centre's Victorian survey, opened), against 22% of renters a year here; 13% had a faulty item in a year (the same survey), against 8% here; 11.5% of the workforce underpaid (McKell Institute, read through a summary: to confirm), against about 6% of employees a year here.
sources.frictions.put_right_on_asking_bps: Asked to put it right, how often the other side does. disrepair: of Victorian renters who reported an issue with their rental provider, 13 in 28 had it unresolved, so 54% resolved (Consumer Policy Research Centre's Victorian survey, opened). goods: 45% of consumers who took action on a problem had it satisfactorily resolved (Australian Consumer Survey 2023, opened). The rest: PLACEHOLDERS standing at the share of people with any problem who say it is done and fully resolved (42.1%: World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only)), which is an outcome of everything people tried, not the rate at which the other side agrees when asked: to replace with a figure by kind of problem.
sources.frictions.pay_short_by_bps: PLACEHOLDER: by how much pay that comes short is short (5%). The Fair Work Ombudsman recovered $473 million for nearly 160,000 workers in 2023-24 (annual report, opened), about $2,960 a worker, which is of that order against a year's pay; no share of pay was found.
sources.frictions.bill_over_bps: PLACEHOLDER: by how much a wrong bill overstates what was used (30%). No figure was found.
sources.frictions.goods_faulty_share_bps: PLACEHOLDER: of a shopping trip's goods, the share that is faulty when some are (a quarter). No figure was found.
sources.frictions.repair_hours: PLACEHOLDER: the hours of a builder's hand a repair takes (two days' work). No figure was found for a typical rental repair.
sources.frictions.support: (Until foundations F6 this note also gave a processing time: a claim for the payment for those out of work took 6 days to process in July 2024, down from 22 early that year (Services Australia annual report 2023-24, opened). It is gone from the town: how long a claim takes is the hours of whoever decides it, and the real agency's wait is not the town's to make; it returns as the time its keepers take to answer, foundations F11.) wrong_refusal_bps: of claims that qualify, the share wrongly refused. FITTED in the 1,000-person town of the first profile (7% of qualifying claims gives about as many refusals a year as 6% of adults, its survey share with difficulty obtaining public benefits, counting the refusals that are right), and for every other place scaled by its own survey share against that one: a stand-in until a place's own rate of decisions changed on review is found. Of Centrelink decisions taken to the Administrative Review Tribunal, 24% were changed (caseload report, 14 Oct 2024 to 30 Jun 2025, opened; the row was inferred: to confirm): a rate among those appealed, not among all refusals. 2026-10-12: this fit assumed every entitled person claims in the year. A town now opens with the payments its people are already entitled to in force (granted before the year, never decided in it), so it decides fewer claims and refuses fewer (Victoria 37.8 to 24.8 a year). It is NOT re-fitted: that would be fitting an outcome again. Reviews of payments in force, which would add wrong stops, were looked for in this place's law and statistics and no rate of wrong stops per review was found; nothing is built (docs/behaviour/frictions.md, 'Payments in force are not reviewed'; docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-12, 'Reviews of payments in force').
sources.founding: Founding (docs/behaviour/founding.md): how often people start something of their own, and the sizes of what they start. Read by the generator only for a town whose spec turns `living.founding` on.
sources.founding.registered_per_100000_per_year: Victoria: 41,590 incorporated associations on the register and about 1,855 new registrations a year (Consumer Affairs Victoria's 2021-22 annual report, as quoted in the Associations Incorporation Reform Regulations 2023 Regulatory Impact Statement, section 1.2; the statement was opened), over about 6.5 million residents (the population is not from that source: to confirm): about 29 per 100,000 a year. Code never reads this figure: it is what chance_bps is fitted to, with informal_multiple.
sources.founding.informal_multiple: PLACEHOLDER (to confirm): how many groups are started for each one that is registered. No count of unregistered groups was found for any place; 5 is a guess (most clubs, circles and tenants' groups never take a legal form). With the registered rate it gives the town's target of new groups per 100,000 residents a year.
sources.founding.chance_bps: FITTED: the chance, at an occasion (a want given up, or with nothing to answer it, that two others share), that a person of the town's mean temperament and standing founds something, set so that a 1,000-person town of this profile has about registered_per_100000_per_year x informal_multiple / 100 new groups a year (docs/behaviour/founding.md has the runs).
sources.founding.sizes: PLACEHOLDERS, every one: shared_min (two others: a critical mass, after Marwell and Oliver 1993, to confirm); rest_days; dues_minutes_of_pay (what a founder may ask a month, as minutes of ordinary pay: nothing, ten minutes, half an hour, an hour; the Los Angeles Tenants Union's own account gives dues averaging five dollars a month, opened, which is of that order); every_days, starts_in_days, lasts_minutes; lapse_days and min_members; leave_after_days; hall_hire_hours_of_pay (two hours of ordinary pay for an evening: no schedule of hall hire was opened); the fund's and the grievance body's rules.
sources.frictions.venues: tribunal_days: the residential tenancies list's median time to finalise, 7 weeks (VCAT annual report 2023-24, opened). answer_days (the time the other side is given to answer a desk), tribunal_fee_hours_of_pay (the fee as hours of a shop worker's pay) and uphold_without_proof_bps (how often a desk finds for someone with nothing to show, where the other side cannot say from its records): PLACEHOLDERS; no figure was opened (VCAT's fee and its outcomes by list are not in the report's narrative).
sources.outlook: How people start out in what they trust (docs/behaviour/citizen.md, 'The record'). National figures for Australia, not the region's: none by region was found. trust: the share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence in each kind of institution (`government`, `policing`: the police, `courts`, the civil service, banks, the press, labour unions, churches or religious organisations, major companies); people_bps: the share who say most people can be trusted. World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7 (fieldwork 2017 to 2022), as Our World in Data publishes it (ourworldindata.org/grapher/trust-state-institutions-wvs, trust-organizations-wvs, self-reported-trust-attitudes), opened 2026-10-11 through a tool that returns a page's figures in summary: to confirm against the survey's own tables. The share is read as the mean level of trust a person starts with, which is a simplification (a share above a threshold is not a mean). Not stated, so the citizen's own placeholders apply (to source: the survey's question on freedom of choice and control over one's life, its mean and spread, needs the microdata): how much control over their lives people feel (outlook.agency). asked.rise_granted_bps: of employees who asked their employer for a pay rise, the share who got one: 20% of men and 16% of women, like for like, in the Australian Workplace Relations Survey 2013-14 (4,600 workers, over 800 employers): Artz, Goodall and Oswald, 'Do Women Ask?', Industrial Relations 57(4), 2018; the University of Warwick's summary of the paper was opened (warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/economics/news/2016/9/new_study_suggests_women_do_ask_for_pay_rises_but_dont_get_them), the paper itself not (to confirm). 18% taken, between the two. National, and a decade old.
sources.outlook.residence: How long people have lived at their current address (starting attachment to the place; docs/behaviour/citizen.md). ABS, 2021 Census, 'Population movement in Australia' (released 8 November 2022; abs.gov.au/articles/population-movement-australia), opened 2026-10-11: 53.1% of the population lived at the same address five years before the Census; 14.3% changed address within Australia in the year before; 0.7% had lived overseas a year before. Bands here: under 1 year = 14.3 + 0.7 = 15.0%; 1 to under 5 = the rest (31.9%); 5 and over = 53.1%. They are built from the one-year and five-year mobility rates, so the 1 to under 5 band is the remainder, and the 5-and-over share is the share at the same address five years earlier (population aged 5 and over, not adults only). National figures, not Victoria's: the Victoria figures were not found on an opened page. The open band is read as 5 to 15 years by the generator.
sources.belief: living_fade_bps_per_month: how fast a belief not kept up fades, a month, in a living town. FITTED to the census's trend in stated affiliation (Christian 52.1% in 2016 and 43.9% in 2021: 1.6 points a year; ABS Census, opened): a living town's gatherings are fuller than a town's without wants, which keeps belief up, and people with initiative turn to a congregation in a loss; the rate the module has (3% a month) was fitted before either. The fit is in docs/decisions.md, 'Everyday frictions'.
sources.job_move: What holds someone in a job they have: another must pay premium_bps more before it is worth moving, and per_year_bps more for each year in the job, up to cap_years; and other_trade_bps more again for a job in another line of work (starting over). FITTED, not sourced figure by figure: set so that the share of employed people who change employer in a year comes near the ABS's (Job mobility, February 2025, opened: 7.7% in the year to February 2025, 8.0% in 2024, 9.6% in 2023), in a town where any better-paid posting was taken before (about 21% a year). The shape has a basis: people who change jobs gain about 9% in pay over those who stay (e61 Institute, read through the trade press: to confirm), so few move for much less; and the chance of leaving a job falls steeply with years in it (Farber 1999, 'Mobility and stability', Handbook of Labor Economics: to confirm). The fit is in docs/decisions.md, 'Everyday frictions'.
sources.outlook.job_tenure: How long employed people have been with their current employer (starting attachment to the trade). OECD, 'Employment by job tenure intervals' (dataset OECD.ELS.SAE DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ, measure TENURE_EMP, share of employment by time with the current employer; both sexes, all ages), national figures for Australia, 2025; read from the OECD SDMX API (sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/OECD.ELS.SAE,DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ) on 2026-10-11, the response opened and the figures copied: under 1 year, 1 to under 3, 3 to under 5, 5 to under 10, 10 and over. National, not the region's: none by region was found. It covers the employed (employees and the self-employed), where a person's tenure is the time in the present job. The open band (10 and over) is read as 10 to 30 years by the generator. The shares sum to 99.9 to 100 in the source and are scaled to 10000. Cross-check, opened 2026-10-11: ABS, Job mobility, February 2026 (released 31 July 2026; abs.gov.au/statistics/labour/jobs/job-mobility/latest-release): under 1 year 16.4%, 1 to 4 years 39.3%, 5 to 9 18.7%, 10 to 19 15.5%, 20 and over 10.0% (employed persons, duration in current job); these agree with the bands used (under 1: 17.1; under 5: 56.8 against 55.7).
sources.knowing.visit_seconds: How long looking at one place takes someone who has gone there (an inspection at a notified stage, a valuer's external look, a welfare check at the door), beside the way there and back. Half an hour: a placeholder. No source was found for any of the three (docs/behaviour/knowing.md, section 3).
sources.knowing.meter_read_seconds: How long reading one water meter takes a reader who has gone to it. Two minutes: a placeholder. No source was found (docs/behaviour/utilities.md, 'Who knows what').
sources.knowing.title_search_fee: What a search of one title costs online: 8.10 (LANDATA service charges 2025-2026, Land Use Victoria, read 2026-10-08 in the Internet Archive's copy of 2026-02-05: 'Folio Search 9.70 20.50 8.10'; the 2026-27 schedule was not reachable). sources.nature.species: Placeholders for growth, mortality, dispersal, min_viable and detection. Gliders and fairy-wrens live in family groups sharing a home range, which isn't modelled, so their breeding threshold is one; frogs breed where at least four share a pond (a home range of half a hectare). How far each crosses ground it can’t live on (dispersal_m): frogs up to 200 m from water (the frog’s guidelines above); gliders glide gaps of tens of metres (75 m, a placeholder); fairy-wrens, placeholder. The young always leave their parents' home range (natal dispersal, in the physics); the share of adults moving a year is a placeholder. Densities and ranges: squirrel glider (listed under Victoria's Flora and Fauna Guarantee Act 1988), 0.38 a hectare in Victoria and a home range of 3-5 ha (van der Ree and others, from the studies summarised in 'Large area used by squirrel gliders in an urban area', PMC8216951; to confirm against the originals), crossing cleared gaps badly; growling grass frog (listed; nationally vulnerable), about 68 adults at a Melbourne wetland (45 males and 23 females, Heard and others; to confirm), moving 15-200 m between waterbodies and living as a metapopulation, sensitive to water quality ('Guidelines for managing the endangered Growling Grass Frog in urbanising landscapes'; the EPBC species profile); superb fairy-wren, a common and conspicuous control, territories of 1-2 ha held by a pair and helpers (Museums Victoria), densities by cover a placeholder.

sources.labour_force_share_by_age: ILOSTAT, 'Labour force participation rate by sex and age (%)', five-year bands (dataflow DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT, https://sdmx.ilo.org/rest/data/ILO,DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT/all?startPeriod=2019; the data file opened and these figures read from it, 2026-10-08), persons, Australia, national, annual 2025, from the ABS Labour Force Survey: ages 25 to 54, 87.003%; 55 to 59, 77.523%; 60 to 64, 61.001%; 65 and over, 16.129%. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track E of docs/design/profile-depth.md): the law is now a list of charges, each with what it is charged on, its schedule, its reliefs and whom it is paid to (docs/behaviour/public-finance.md). Two charges, the same figures: the resident rates on a year's pay, and the levy on the whole of a pay from its threshold. Nothing is changed; both are paid to the general government.
sources.public_finance.returns: [RECALLED, to confirm] ATO: a medium withholder (AUD 25,001 to 1 million a year, per business.gov.au, opened) reports and pays PAYG withholding monthly on the activity statement, due the 21st of the following month; a small withholder (AUD 25,000 or less) does so quarterly (28 Oct, 28 Feb, 28 Apr, 28 Jul), not used here; the Medicare levy is withheld within the PAYG amount. The ATO's own page (paying-and-reporting-payg-withholding-amounts-for-small-and-medium-withholders) returned an access error, so the days are recalled, not read.
sources.public_finance.grants_per_resident_per_y: Derived: Victoria's 2025-26 general purpose financial assistance grants, $612.0M (Victorian Local Government Grants Commission, 2025-26 annual allocation report, tabled September 2025), over Victoria's population, about 6.98 million (ABS, National, state and territory population, 2025; to confirm). Local roads grants ($218.3M) are left out: the town has no roads yet.
sources.public_finance.rates_per_resident_per_ye: Derived: Victorian councils' rates and charges, 51% of $15.3B revenue in 2024-25 (VAGO, Results of 2024-25 Audits: Local Government), over about 6.9 million residents: about $1,131 a resident a year (to confirm). Sets the town's opening rate in the dollar.
sources.public_finance.rates_instalments: Local Government Act 1989 (Vic), s 167: rates are payable in four instalments (or as a lump sum).
sources.public_finance.rates_due_days: Placeholder: an instalment falls due 30 days after its notice.
sources.public_finance.rates_penalty_interest_bp: Local Government Act 1989 (Vic), s 172: interest on unpaid rates at the rate fixed under the Penalty Interest Rates Act 1983, 10% a year (to confirm the current rate).
sources.public_finance.rates_exempt_kinds: Land used exclusively for charitable, educational or public health purposes is not rateable (Local Government Act 1989 (Vic), s 154; to confirm): here, the clinic's, the school's, the police station's (Crown land) and the utilities' (land used for water supply is exempt; the energy retailer's substation is treated alike, a liberty).
sources.public_finance.median_house_price: Valuer-General Victoria, A Guide to Property Values 2024 (released July 2025): country Victoria's median house price, $572,000. The land value of a lot is derived from it: this less what the builder charges to build a house.
sources.services.waste_per_person_per_day_g: Derived: 512 kg of municipal solid waste per person a year, 2022-23 (DCCEEW, National Waste and Resource Recovery Report 2024), a day's worth in grams.
sources.services.landfill_levy_per_tonne: EPA Victoria, waste levy 2025-26: municipal waste in rural areas, $84.78 a tonne. What the landfill charges on top (its gate fee) is left out.
sources.services.council_staff_per_1000: Derived: about 40,600 FTE in Victorian councils at 30 June 2023 (Vic Councils, Local government facts) over about 6.9 million residents: about 6 per 1,000 (to confirm against the MAV workforce report). In the town, all of them are its works crew.
sources.services.collect_seconds_per_10kg: Placeholder: a one-driver side-loader lifts up to 6 bins a minute (Bucher Municipal, Sport side loader); with driving between houses, about 1,000 bins a day is taken as a round, and a household's week of waste as about 24 kg: about 12 seconds of work per 10 kg.
sources.services.asset_life_years: Placeholder: a park or civic building wears out in 15 years without upkeep (after VAGO, Maintaining Local Roads: spray seals last 10-15 years).
sources.services.upkeep_hours_per_week_per_asset: Placeholder: a crew member's half a day a week keeps a park or the hall up (mowing, bins, repairs).
sources.services.complain_bps: Placeholder: the chance a week that a household whose waste has gone two weeks uncollected writes to the town. Who reports and who doesn't varies (the service-request literature, e.g. Stowers 2022, State and Local Government Review); a rate is to be sourced.
sources.public_service.wage_per_pay_period: [MIXED] Victorian Local Government Award 2015 (MA000132) Level 4 minimum was about $1,068 a week in 2025 (FWC wage draft; opened via search), about $1,119 after the 4.75% 2026 review; councils' enterprise agreements pay clerical Band 4 officers above the award, roughly $78-85k a year. Taken as $80,000 a year, $3,077 a fortnight (to confirm against a council EA).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.administra: [MIXED] Victoria's 79 councils employ about 37,000 EFT (MAV local government facts, search summary) for 6.9m people, about 5.4 per 1,000; the profile's works/waste crew takes part of that. Administration set at 3.0, about 55% of the total, after leaving out works, libraries and community services (share estimated, to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.courts: [PLACEHOLDER] VCAT (civil and residential tenancies lists) has about 600 staff plus several hundred full- and part-time members for 6.9m residents; annual report 2024-25 not opened for numbers. Estimated 0.12 per 1,000, with the Magistrates' Court civil list partly counted.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.oversight: [PLACEHOLDER] Victorian Ombudsman (about 130 staff) plus the consumer-affairs regulator and dispute-resolution staff (a few hundred, shared with other work) over 6.9m residents. Estimated 0.06 per 1,000; headcounts from memory, not opened.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.elections: [PLACEHOLDER] The Victorian Electoral Commission keeps roughly 250 permanent staff outside election periods (from memory, to confirm) for 6.9m residents, about 0.036 per 1,000.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.land_regis: [PLACEHOLDER] Land Use Victoria's titles and registry work is roughly 300 staff statewide (estimate, to confirm); over 6.9m residents it is about 0.045 per 1,000.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.press: [PLACEHOLDER] A regional or suburban local paper serving about 20,000 people with a three-person editorial team (editor and two reporters) gives 0.15 per 1,000; typical of small Australian mastheads, not from a dataset.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.banking: [PLACEHOLDER] Australian banks and credit unions employ about 150,000 people for 27m residents (5.5 per 1,000), most in head offices and call centres. A local retail bank's branch, lending and payments staff set at 2.5 per 1,000; estimate, ABS and APRA figures not opened.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.utilities: [PLACEHOLDER] Victoria's metropolitan and regional water corporations employ about 6,000 for 6.9m people (about 0.9 per 1,000); a retailer's operations add roughly 0.3. Total 1.2, estimated from memory of corporation annual reports (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.union: [PLACEHOLDER] About 1.4m Victorian union members; roughly 1 paid officer or organiser per 1,500-2,000 members across unions gives about 700-900 staff, but local organisers are fewer. Set at 0.15 per 1,000; no source opened.
sources.public_service.licences.payment_system: [PLACEHOLDER] A core-banking and payments platform costs a small bank an estimated A$10-20 per customer a year in vendor fees; taken as $15 (1,500 cents) per resident. No vendor price list found; honest guess.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.property_m: [PLACEHOLDER] Carried over unchanged to every profile: property managers (people who run let homes for their owners) at about one to every 100 to 150 let homes is an industry rule of thumb (to confirm, not opened); a town here has about 380 homes for 1,000 people, so about 3 per 1,000 residents. A manager looks after the letting offices of several landlords.
sources.public_service.appointed_by: [PLACEHOLDER] Who fills the post of a public body when none of its own staff is left: the town's council, which seconds one of its own staff to it, as a local government assigns officers to bodies it runs. Real places mostly give these appointments to a state body, a minister or a board, none of which the town models, so the council stands in for them (to confirm per place). Bodies run on their own account (the bank, the union, the paper, landlords, shops) are not covered: their owners or members would appoint, and no owner's or member's office exists to do it.
sources.unions.membership_bps: ABS, Trade union membership, August 2024: 13.1% of employees; by industry, manufacturing 9.0%, construction 11.7%, retail trade 7.0%, public administration and safety 23.1% (the industry figures to confirm against the release's tables); `other`, the overall rate. Keyed by the industries employers' postings name.
sources.unions.resignation_notice_days: Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Act 2009 (Cth), s 174: a member may resign by written notice, which takes effect two weeks after it's received (or at once, if the member is no longer eligible; to confirm against the section). Written into each membership as the member's notice.
sources.groups.leave_notice_days: Placeholder: a member may leave a club or congregation at once (a voluntary association; a club's own rules may ask for notice). Written into each membership as the member's notice.
sources.unions.dues_per_month: Placeholder: about $14 a week, around what large Australian unions charge full-time members (to source).
sources.unions.claim_margin_bps: Placeholder: a union claims the year's rise in prices and 2% more. Settlements are measured against the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations' Trends in Federal Enterprise Bargaining (average annualised wage increases in new agreements), a calibration target.
sources.households.age_bands_bps: ABS, Census 2021 QuickStats, Rest of Vic. (GCCSA 2RVIC): people by five-year age group (median age 43); 85 and over taken to 99. The ages of adults living alone, as couples without children at home, or in groups are drawn from this, less the parents the family shares imply (the generator derives it: docs/behaviour/households.md).
sources.unions.meeting_every_days: Placeholder: a members' meeting a month.
sources.groups.kinds: The kinds of social group the ABS General Social Survey counts (sport or physical recreation; religious or spiritual; arts or heritage; craft or practical hobby; other recreational or special interest: the category list to confirm against the survey's glossary). How often each meets, and for how long, are placeholders. Whether people come is theirs: the survey's participation is a calibration target (targets), not a rate given to anyone.
sources.groups.taking_part_bps: Calibrated (2026-09-30): the share of adults who belong to a group at the start (which kind: evenly, a placeholder) and go to its gatherings; after that, whether anyone goes is theirs. The survey counts anyone who took part over 12 months (ABS, General Social Survey 2019: 50.0% of people aged 18 and over), which is more than belong at any one time, so it is the target (targets), not this share. At 50% here, a year's participation came out at 60%.
sources.groups.kinds.teaching: What a group asks people to hold, in its words: content, for belief to attach to (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 5). The congregation's stands for the Christian denominations together (one congregation per town is a simplification).
sources.groups.kinds.held_at_start_bps: ABS, Census of Population and Housing 2021: 43.9% of people reported a Christian affiliation (to confirm against the release; other religions, 10.0%, aren't represented yet). At the start, the congregation's members hold its teaching strongly, and others up to this share hold it less; after that it strengthens, spreads and fades.
sources.unions.teaching: The union movement's claim, in words (content for belief). Its members hold it at the start.
sources.groups.per_kind_per_1000_people: Placeholder: one group of each kind for every 1,000 people.
sources.households.child_max_age: The census counts children of any age living with their parents; the ABS family coding counts full-time students to 24 as dependent children. Children at home are drawn up to 24 (a simplification: older children at home are left out).
